Dogecoin in 2025: Still Standing

Despite its meme origins, DOGE still has traction:

• Over 1M daily transactions
• Market cap: $25.7B
• Ranked #9 on CoinMarketCap
• Price: ~$0.17, up 24% in a month

The joke coin is still alive - and thriving. https://t.co/OMm4TSoWr2

Starting in 2020, Elon began tweeting memes and support for Dogecoin.

➔ Dec 2020: “One word: Doge” ➔ DOGE +20%
➔ Feb 2021: “Dogecoin is the people’s crypto” ➔ DOGE +40%
➔ April 2021: Tweeted “Doge Barking at the Moon” ➔ DOGE +100%
➔ In 2023 he Changed Twitter logo to

Then the Explosion Began…

In 2020–2021, Dogecoin came roaring back.

Reddit, TikTok, and Elon Musk pushed it into orbit.

At its peak, DOGE was worth $0.74 and had a $85B market cap.

Billy? He watched from the sidelines… in a Honda. https://t.co/lblk56YI5C

Exit Before the Moon

By 2015, Dogecoin’s fun culture was fading.

Greed crept in. Scammers showed up. Billy got burned out.

So he left the project - and sold all his coins.

The ~33M DOGE? Gone for the price of a used Honda Civic. https://t.co/TOEWAkRvSX

Dogecoin Was Never Supposed to Succeed

It launched in December 2013 as a parody of Bitcoin.

No roadmap. No VC backing. Just vibes.

But the internet loved it.

Dogecoin quickly surpassed Bitcoin in daily transactions - all from pure meme energy. https://t.co/VEAztW2hXV

From IBM Engineer ➔ Meme Coin Creator

In 2013, Billy Markus was working as a software dev at IBM.

He found a tweet joking about a “DogeCoin.”

Inspired by the Shiba meme, he turned the joke into real code - just for fun.

A few hours later, Dogecoin was born. https://t.co/JAb8E2OCh2

$DOGE started as a joke to him!

He sold everything (~33M DOGE for $10K) to buy a used Honda Civic.

Meanwhile, Dogecoin hit a $70B market cap, and he lost ~$20M

Here’s the full story of Billy Markus - and what every trader needs to learn from it 🧵👇 https://t.co/6W88tbmudF
